The climate in Borovets

Borovets is about 1320 m above sea level. The warmest month is August, with an average high of 22°C; the coldest is January, when nights average −6°C. Around 1120 mm of precipitation falls in a year on average, most of it in June (about 153 mm). The highest temperature in Borovets in 2015–2024 was 32°C (25 July 2023) and the lowest −24°C (23 January 2016).

Borovets lies on the northern slopes of Rila at about 1300 m and is the oldest mountain resort in Bulgaria. Snow usually lies from December to April, and it is colder still above the resort, on the runs towards Yastrebets. Summers are cool and rarely hot, with frequent afternoon showers in the mountains.

Best time to visit Borovets

The most pleasant weather in Borovets is usually in July and August: average highs are around 22°C, with up to 11 days of rain a month. In January, February and December nights are frosty (below −3°C on average) and snow is common.
